venue: Student Union Ballroom, U. of Utah

ai_show_review.summary: Explosive Dark Star > The Eleven chain with soaring Lovelight
ai_show_review.blurb: Late‑show set delivers a blistering Dark Star that segues into Saint Stephen and a kinetic The Eleven. Turn On Your Lovelight erupts with raw, analog heat, while the recording captures the band’s high‑energy vibe despite a few splice‑related cuts.
ai_show_review.review:
The April 12, 1969 late set at the University of Utah’s Student Union Ballroom finds the Dead firing on all cylinders. Jerry’s agitation at a non‑dancing crowd translates into a ferocious Dark Star that stretches and twists before launching straight into Saint Stephen and the relentless, rhythm‑shifting The Eleven. From there the band rides a bright current into Turn On Your Lovelight, where Pigpen’s soulful organ and Tom Constanten’s textural keys add perfect color to the soaring guitar lines, before the night ends in a wild burst of feedback. Though the soundboard tape bears some analog hiss, speed‑adjusted splices, and missing fragments of The Other One and Too, the overall clarity remains solid and the performance’s intensity shines through.

For listeners seeking an authentic snapshot of the Dead’s 1969 live fire, this recording offers a vivid portrait: high energy, adventurous improvisation, and that unmistakable vintage tape character. It may not be flawless, but the musical moments are compelling enough to make it a must‑hear for fans of early Dark Star explorations.

best_recording.reason: Soundboard source with good overall clarity, capturing the high‑energy performance despite vintage hiss and a few splice‑related cuts.

key_highlights: Ferocious Dark Star that drives the set into an inspired Saint Stephen transition
The Eleven’s relentless rhythmic propulsion showcases tight interplay
Turn On Your Lovelight erupts with raw, analog heat and vibrant organ texture
Overall high‑energy vibe preserved despite minor tape splices and missing fragments

band_performance.Jerry: Agitated by a non‑dancing crowd, Jerry channels that tension into an intense, fiery guitar lead throughout Dark Star and the subsequent jams.
